metadata.title: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was limited at a second-straight practice on Thursday. He's still dealing with a groin injury, and it's possible that it will force him to miss another game this week. We should know more about his official status after practice on Friday.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Allen (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: It was another limited session for Allen, who is working his way back from a groin injury that kept him out against the Commanders in Week 4. Allen is trending toward being ready to go against the Steelers on Sunday, which would give this receiving corps a much-needed boost.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Allen (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: After missing last Sunday's win over the Commanders, Allen's return to the practice field puts him on track to suit up Sunday against the Steelers. He should slot back into full-time duties alongside Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell, with Ashton Dulin heading back to more of a special-teams role.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout was limited by a groin injury on Wednesday, which isn't surprising after that same issue left him sidelined in Week 4. It remains to be seen whether or not he will play on Sunday, but either way he shouldn't be viewed as a strong fantasy option.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Returns to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Allen (groin) will practice Wednesday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: After sitting out the Week 4 loss to the Commanders in London, Allen's ability to practice in some fashion to begin Week 5 prep puts him on a good track to play this Sunday against the Steelers. With Alec Pierce (heel) still on injured reserve, the Colts need all the help they can get at receiver after Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin (hamstring) were forced into heavy snaps alongside Josh Downs in Week 4.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Practicing on Wednesday
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (groin) is participating in practice on Wednesday, according to James Boyd of The Athletic. Allen was not cleared to play in London in Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders due to a groin injury, but the 34-year-old veteran's return to practice on Wednesday suggests he is tracking towards a return in Week 5 to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road. It is good news for a Colts offense that still has top receiver Alec Pierce (heel) on Injured Reserve. If Allen is cleared to play this Sunday in the Steel City, he should be quarterback Daniel Jones' WR2 behind Josh Downs. Allen caught only seven passes for 37 yards in the first two games of the 2026 season in his first year with the team, but he picked things up in the Week 3 win over the division-rival Houston Texans by catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first touchdown of the year. If Allen is active this weekend against the Steelers, he will be in play as a WR4/flex in deeper fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen (groin) out for Week 4
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Allen has been listed as questionable on Friday, but the veteran will indeed sit out Sunday's game. With both Allen and Alec Pierce out of action, the Colts are very thin at wide receiver. Look for Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren to be heavily targeted by QB Daniel Jones. Veterans Laquon Treadwell and Darius Slayton could be in the mix as well.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Ruled out for Sunday
metadata.description: Allen (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against Washington.
metadata.analysis: After entering the weekend with a questionable tag following a non-participant listing Friday, Allen will now miss Sunday's contest in London. Without Allen nor Alec Pierce (heel), Josh Downs will be the Colts' top receiver for Week 4, with Darius Slayton, Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Deion Burks and tight end Tyler Warren all in line for more targets. Allen's next chance to take the field is Week 5 against the Steelers on Sunday, Oct. 11.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Ruled Out for Week 4
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's Week 4 contest against the Washington Commanders in London, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN.com. Wide receiver injuries continue to plague the Colts, who had already placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve earlier in the season. Allen being inactive is a major loss for the Colts, given that he exploded for six catches, 63 yards, and one touchdown last weekend. Now, this Daniel Jones-led passing attack will take on the Commanders with a wide receiver group led by Josh Downs, Darius Slayton, Laquon Treadwell, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, and Ashton Dulin (ankle). metadata.title: Keenan Allen (groin) officially questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (groin) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Allen was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Friday and is officially questionable for Sunday's game as a result. If he is sidelined, fantasy managers should expect Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin (ankle) to both see more work as a result of his absence.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Questionable for Week 4
metadata.description: Allen (groin) was listed as a non-participant for Friday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
metadata.analysis: After logging a limited practice Thursday, Allen moved the wrong direction Friday with a DNP tag and now carries a questionable designation into Sunday's contest in London. That leaves the Colts' veteran wide receiver with some added uncertainty for Week 4 availability. If Allen is unable to go, the Colts will dip even deeper into their wideout depth with Alec Pierce (heel) already on the shelf for multiple weeks. Josh Downs and Tyler Warren would be in line to soak up most of the targets.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Questionable to Play in Week 4 with Groin Injury
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (groin) is officially questionable to play in his team's Week 4 matchup against the Washington Commanders with a groin injury, per Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star. Allen is coming off his best game of the young season, recording six catches for 63 yards and a touchdown on nine targets in Week 3 against the Houston Texans. With Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) currently on Injured Reserve, a healthy Allen profiles as the team's WR2 alongside Josh Downs. However, Allen was listed as a non-participant in the Colts' walkthrough on Friday and could be in real danger of being inactive on Sunday. If Allen is sidelined, Downs and Colts tight end Tyler Warren could absolutely dominate the team's target share in Week 4 against Washington.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) limited at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran is dealing with some kind of a minor groin injury, which contributed to him being a limited participant at Thursday's practice. It's not currently thought to be much of an issue for him, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on what his injury status ends up being heading into the weekend.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Limited by groin injury
metadata.description: Allen was a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to a groin injury.
metadata.analysis: The veteran receiver was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice due to rest, but an injury played a part in his restrictions a day later. With that in mind, Allen may need to turn in a full practice Friday to approach Sunday's game against the Commanders in London without an injury designation. Allen is coming off his best performance of the season in Week 3, when he turned in a 6-63-1 receiving line on nine targets in a 19-17 win over the Texans.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen a Top Waiver-Wire Target with Teammate Sidelined
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen took advantage of increased opportunities on Sunday, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and one touchdown. Allen took on a larger role in the passing game with Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve. Since Pierce will be sidelined through at least Week 6, Allen should remain on the fantasy radar for at least a few more games. His nine targets and 74% snap share Sunday suggest that quarterback Daniel Jones is very comfortable throwing him the football, and we've already seen that he can co-exist with fellow wide receiver Josh Downs, who had five catches on 11 targets in Week 3. Given that Allen can be started as a WR3/flex in Week 4, he's a very intriguing waiver wire target for fantasy managers in most leagues.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Records touchdown in win
metadata.description: Allen caught six of nine targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Allen was able to take advantage of the absence of Alec Pierce (heel) in Week 3, matching his season-high six receptions while notching his first touchdown of the year in the second quarter on a six-yard pass from Daniel Jones. With Pierce set to miss extended time, Allen will have a chance to carve out a significant role for himself as a reliable option for Indianapolis.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen finds the end zone in Week 3
metadata.description: Keenan Allen caught 6-of-9 targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in a 19-17 win over the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Allen turned in his best performance of the season and found the end zone for the first time as a Colt. With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve, fantasy managers should expect Allen to see an increase in playing time. Allen and the Colts will take on the Commanders in Week 4.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen A Potential Deep-League Option In Week 3
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen will be thrust into a bigger role due to the injury to Colts WR1 Alec Pierce (heel). He could have enough targets to be startable in deep leagues for Week 3, though that's a risky prospect considering his production so far this season. Through two games, he has only seven receptions for 37 yards and zero touchdowns. He's been targeted 11 times so far, which is somewhat encouraging, but he hasn't been a downfield threat at all. And in Week 3, the Houston Texans' defense is likely to make it tough on him to do much more than rack up a few PPR fantasy points from catches. Allen is 34 years old, and while he showed upside last season, it could be that this is the year it falls apart for him. WRs of his age almost never have consistent season-long production or dominant games against some of the NFL's best defenses. Outside of deep dynasty leagues, Allen should be left on the bench or on waivers until he proves we should do otherwise.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen held to one catch Sunday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen caught 1-of-5 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: The veteran saw five opportunities on Sunday night, but he was only able to haul in one catch for five yards over the course of the night. He hasn't looked very good over the first two games of the season, which mitigates a lot of the optimism surrounding him now that Alec Pierce (heel) seems set to miss time.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Poised for Larger Role in Colts Passing Game?
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen had a disappointing game in his team's Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, recording one catch for five yards on five targets. However, the 34-year-old has played a consistent role in his team's offense early in 2026, logging 11 targets through two games. Allen's role may be poised to grow coming out of Week 2, as Colts wideout Alec Pierce (heel) had to leave the team's loss to the Chiefs on a cart after re-aggravating an existing heel injury. While X-rays came back negative on Pierce's left heel, he underwent surgery on his left ankle over the offseason and has been dealing with complications in the area ever since. At this point in his career, Allen does not carry a ton of explosive production upside. However, the veteran wide receiver has always been a consistent target earner, and he could establish himself as a high-floor PPR option for deep-league managers to target on the waiver wire.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Held to one catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Allen caught one of five targets for five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Allen failed to capitalize on the first-half exit of fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel). Dating back to last season with the Chargers, the 34-year-old Allen is mired in a 12-game regular-season touchdown drought, during which he has exceeded 44 receiving yards only once. Snapping that funk won't be easy in Week 3 against the Texans.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Targeted Five Times, Held To One Catch In Week 2 Loss
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen caught just one of his five targets for five yards in a Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has now seen 11 targets across two games, so it's not like he isn't being involved in the game plan. He just has struggled to turn those looks into good production. That comes with the territory of being 34 years old and still playing in the NFL. Allen could have a bigger role in the coming weeks, though, with WR Alec Pierce (heel) struggling with a re-aggravation of the heel injury that bothered him in the offseason. Allen is now a top-2 WR, depth chart-wise at least, in an offense that's depleted of pass-catching weapons. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown an average of just 188 yards per game over the first two contests, meaning there hasn't been much to go around for the team's pass-catchers. Allen moves into borderline WR4 territory for Week 3 against the tough Houston Texans defense. He's likely in his last year in the NFL, and is a shadow of his former self. He could still get enough targets and receptions to be startable in PPR leagues, though.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Facing league suspension
metadata.description: Allen "is facing a minimum three-game suspension" in connection with his August arrest, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Allen was formally charged with two misdemeanors last week after being arrested on DUI charges in late August, and the NFL could levy a suspension of three games or more for his actions. Per the report, "Allen is not expected to miss playing time while the case proceeds through the courts."

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Facing a Three-Game Suspension
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen is facing a minimum three-game suspension following his drunk driving arrest last month, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN.com. He reports that there's also a chance the suspension could be for more than three games, which is permitted by the NFL's collective bargaining agreement for scenarios when the player is intoxicated at higher levels. A more severe ban is definitely possible, given that Allen's .224 blood-alcohol level at the scene was more than three times the legal limit. Allen signed with the Colts late in the offseason, slotting into the No. 3 role. He was heavily involved in Week 1, catching six passes for 32 yards. His volume could decrease a little in Week 2 now that Alec Pierce (heel) is fully healthy, but he's still worth considering as a WR3/flex in deeper PPR leagues until he gets suspended.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen (rest) full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (rest) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.

He may see more work than usual if Alec Pierce (heel) or Ashton Dulin (ankle) are sidelined against Kansas City.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen (rest) officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Keenan Allen (rest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.

The team is intentionally limiting his workload at the start of the practice week, however, so it's nothing that fantasy managers should be concerned with. He should play in Week 2 but projects to be a weaker fantasy option in a tough matchup against the Chiefs this week.

metadata.title: Keenan Allen - Formally facing charges
metadata.description: Allen has been formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his August arrest, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
metadata.analysis: Allen was arrested in late August, and he has officially been charged with two counts, including "OVWI with a BAC of .15 or more." Per the same source, "The NFL's policy says an eight-game suspension could be levied with aggravating circumstances (including 'extreme intoxication' with a BAC of .15 or more)."

metadata.title: Keenan Allen Formally Charged With Two Misdemeanors
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has formally been charged following his Aug. 30 arrest, according to Mike Chappell. Court records show Allen is facing two misdemeanor counts, one for operating a vehicle while intoxicated and another for operating a vehicle with an alcohol concentration equivalent to 0.15 or more. The charges replace the preliminary allegations reported after his arrest, though the case remains ongoing and Allen has not been convicted. There has been no new NFL discipline announced. Allen was available for Indianapolis in Week 1 and caught all six of his targets for 32 yards in the loss to Baltimore. For now, his fantasy status does not change, but managers should keep an eye on the situation in case the league takes action later in the legal process.
